Q: How to generate truly random numbers (NOT pseudo) in Linux A:

You can read from /dev/random which is populated with an entropy pool. There is some good info on the Wikipedia article about it.

Q: Dataframe sorting and column count A:

Use .size().reset_index(name='Count') instead of .agg({'CoffeeType':'count'}), and convert the DayOfWeek column into a categorical type with a custom Monday-to-Sunday order.

import pandas as pd

# Define the correct order for days of the week
day_order = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday']

# Convert DayOfWeek to a categorical type with that order
coffee_dataset['DayOfWeek'] = pd.Categorical(
    coffee_dataset['DayOfWeek'], 
    categories=day_order, 
    ordered=True
)

# Group, count, rename the column, and sort by the custom order
result = (
    coffee_dataset.groupby(['DayOfWeek', 'CoffeeType'], observed=False)
    .size()
    .reset_index(name='Count')
    .sort_values(['DayOfWeek', 'CoffeeType'])
)

print(result)

Q: How can I copy files from a host to a Docker container? A:

There are overly complicated answers, but this worked for me:

To copy from the host to a container:

docker cp HOSTPATH CONTAINER:PATH

Q: How can I let Visual Studio Code open file using the default program of the operating system? A:

There are two extensions that I know of (no affiliation) that tackle this problem:

  • Open in External App

    ... with this extension, you can do it more simply. Just right-click to the file, and select Open in External App. That file would be opened by the system default application. You can also use this way to open .psd files with Photoshop, .html files with browser, and so on...

    The configuration implies that you need to manually set which application to use for which extension, so it doesn't simply use the default configured in your OS (at least not in my brief test).

  • Open

    Opens files using the OS's default program for the file type

    This does what it says out of the box, but the keyboard shortcut seems to fail. The command can only be triggered via the right-click menu of the file in the Visual Studio Code file browser.

Q: How to take backup of Mysql databases in XAMPP without using phpmyadmin A:

Short Answer: Yes, you will be able to recover.

  1. Copy content from your /installation_path/xampp/mysql directory to your desired location.
  2. ReInstall and copy back the content.
  3. Restart your services.

[or]

If you have your backup in a Folder, do the following:

datadir = "your/path/mysql/backupdata"

in xampp/mysql/bin/my.ini

Q: Error:Execution failed for task ':app:compileReleaseJavaWithJavac'. > Compilation failed; see the compiler error output for details A:

I hope my answer is not late. Recently I was facing exactly same issue, I was trying to make an apk release build but I was getting same error message as you. In other side the app is working perfectly in debug mode. I figured out that my proguard-rules file is missing some rules because I was enabling the obfuscation in the release mode. you have to double check if you proguard-rules is up to date. before make any update, try first disable the obfuscation from gradle file or by adding -dontobfuscate to your proguard-rules, if the issue will disappear that means you will have to update you gradle file with your own appropriate rules.
